memos.headline: Mega-cap tech breaks down while JPM, UNH, and CAT hold leadership — rotation favors non-tech
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe this week. The big-five tech names (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL) are all trading well below their 50-day means with RSIs in the 33–41 range and 4-week relative strength vs SPY ranging from -5.8% to -11.7%, signaling broad-based distribution. MSFT is the weakest, sitting 16.7% below its 200-day mean and 31.2% off its 52-week high — a structural downtrend I want no part of. On the other side, JPM is within 1.8% of its 52-week high with a healthy RSI of 60 and +14.3% 4-week relative strength; CAT is a parabolic leader at +77.5% over 26 weeks and +45.6% above its 200-day mean, though that extension raises mean-reversion risk; and UNH just printed a new 52-week high with RSI 71.5 and +46% 12-week relative strength — the strongest chart in the group but overbought enough to warrant a tight leash. I'd buy JPM on any dip toward its 50-day mean (~$311), stay long UNH above $400, and avoid the tech cluster until RSIs reclaim 50 and prices retake their 50-day averages.

views.note: Near 52-week highs, RSI 60, strong 4-week relative strength of +14.3% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below ~$311 (50-day mean area).
New 52-week high with dominant relative strength (+46% 12w vs SPY), but RSI 71.5 is overbought — would cut on a close below $400.
Massive momentum (+77.5% 26w, +28.7% 12w rel strength) but extremely extended at +45.6% above 200-day mean; trail stops tight near $950.
Structural downtrend: -31.2% from 52-week high, -16.7% below 200-day mean, persistent negative relative strength; no reason to step in until price reclaims ~$410.

RSI 33.3 is the lowest in the universe and price is -8.6% below 50-day mean; 12-week relative strength is still positive so this could be a pullback in an uptrend, but I want to see RSI back above 45 before engaging.
Down 15.1% in 4 weeks with -11.7% relative strength vs SPY; sitting right on its 200-day mean which is the line — a close below $230 confirms further downside.
RSI 37.5 and -8.4% below 50-day mean suggest oversold bounce potential, but 4-week relative strength is -6.7%; would turn long on a reclaim of the 50-day (~$210).
Low-volatility name hugging its 200-day mean with RSI 53 — no edge either way; useful as a defensive hold but not a momentum trade.
Down 19.5% over 12 weeks with -31.6% relative strength vs SPY — the worst relative performer in the group; RSI 33.9 is oversold but trend is clearly broken.
Still above its 200-day mean by 5.3% but weakening near-term with RSI 41 and -5.8% 4-week relative strength; watching $275 as support — a break below flips me to avoid.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Deliver Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and UNH Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I am most convicted on the names showing durable, accelerating earnings power and least comfortable where margins are compressing into commodity or regulatory headwinds. NVDA's 2027Q1 print is staggering—$81.6B revenue (+85% YoY) with a 71.5% net margin and only $8.5B total debt, producing $58.3B net income (+211% YoY)—this is the cleanest earnings story in the universe. GOOGL posted $110B revenue (+22% YoY) with net margin expanding to 56.9% and net income surging 81%, on a balance sheet carrying just $14.8B debt; I want to own that margin trajectory. On the other side, XOM's net income collapsed 46% YoY to $4.2B on essentially flat revenue (+2.4%), compressing net margin to 4.9%—I see no catalyst to reverse that without a commodity price recovery. UNH's revenue growth stalled at +2.0% with net income flat at $6.3B and a 5.6% net margin against $77.9B of debt; the earnings power here looks fragile, and any uptick in medical cost ratios would change the picture further.

views.note: Revenue +85% YoY, net margin 71.5%, net income +211% YoY on minimal leverage ($8.5B debt)—unmatched earnings momentum.
Net income +81% YoY to $62.6B with 56.9% net margin and only $14.8B debt signals durable, expanding profitability.
Revenue +18% YoY, net margin 38.3%, net income +23% YoY with moderate $40B debt—steady compounder I'm happy to own.
Net income +77% YoY to $30.3B and margin expansion to 16.7% are encouraging, though $122.6B total debt warrants monitoring.
Solid +17% revenue growth and 26.6% net margin, but $82.7B debt and slower earnings growth (+19%) versus peers temper enthusiasm.
Revenue +22% and net income +27% are strong, but 14.6% net margin and $36.2B debt leave limited margin of safety if cyclical demand fades.
Revenue +10% and net income +13% are respectable for a bank, but the massive $449B debt stack and rate-cycle sensitivity keep me on the sideline.
Steady 18.5% net margin and +7% revenue growth offer defensiveness, but +4% earnings growth doesn't excite at current multiples.
Net income down 46% YoY to $4.2B with a 4.9% net margin on flat revenue—clear earnings compression I don't want to own.
Revenue growth of just +2% and flat net income at $6.3B against $77.9B debt signals stalling earnings power; a rising MLR would worsen the picture.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 3.75% as Sticky 4.2% YoY CPI Stalls Further Easing—Favor Defensives Over Duration
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has sat at 3.75% for three months despite 75 bps of cuts over the past year, and headline CPI running at +4.2% YoY (May print 333.98) gives the FOMC no room to move. The labor market is stable with unemployment at 4.3%, down 10 bps over three months and flat YoY, so there is no urgency to ease further on the employment side. The 10y-2y spread has compressed 18 bps over three months to just +0.31 pp, signaling the market is pricing slower growth or a prolonged pause rather than renewed easing. I have moderate conviction that this pause-with-sticky-inflation regime favors cash-flow-rich defensives and banks earning on a still-positive curve, while it pressures high-duration growth names and cyclicals sensitive to a flattening curve. A CPI print falling below 3% annualized or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would flip my regime call toward renewed easing and a growth-stock tilt.

views.note: Duration-sensitive mega-cap growth faces headwinds from a 4.38% 10y and no near-term rate relief, but stable earnings keep it from an outright avoid.
High-multiple growth is capped by sticky inflation and a prolonged Fed pause; I need to see CPI decelerate before turning constructive.
A positive 10y-2y spread of 31 bps and stable unemployment at 4.3% support net interest margins and credit quality in a pause regime.
Defensive staples with pricing power benefit from a sticky-inflation, pause-rate environment where consumers still spend on essentials.
Energy is a partial inflation hedge but the flattening curve and stable labor market suggest no demand surge; I lack conviction either way.
Cyclicals face the most risk from a flattening curve (10y-2y down 18 bps in 3 months) and a Fed unwilling to ease further amid 4.2% inflation.
Consumer hardware giant is caught between resilient demand (4.3% unemployment) and valuation pressure from elevated long rates at 4.38%.
Healthcare defensive with stable cash flows benefits in a pause regime; low sensitivity to rate moves and steady employment support utilization.

memos.headline: Filing Cadence Signals: GOOGL and JPM Show Elevated Activity, NVDA Post-Earnings Drift Negative
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and associated price reactions across the universe as a proxy for narrative intensity, since I lack direct GDELT tone data in this evidence set. GOOGL stands out with six 8-K filings in roughly five weeks—including material definitive agreements, bylaw amendments, and board changes—suggesting a governance or strategic narrative shift that could attract incremental media coverage and sentiment volatility. JPM is similarly active with seven filings since early May, culminating in a board change on 2026-06-25 and dual filings on 2026-06-24; this volume often precedes or accompanies heightened media tone, though the filings themselves appear routine. NVDA's earnings 8-K on 2026-05-20 drew a -1.8% next-day reaction, and the subsequent 'Other Events' filing on 2026-06-18 suggests the narrative has not yet turned positive—I see no catalyst for a sentiment inflection. XOM's Q1 results on 2026-05-01 produced a -1.0% move and the filing flow has been quiet since late May, consistent with a fading negative tone that could stabilize sentiment.

views.note: Unusually high filing cadence with governance changes and material agreements creates sentiment uncertainty; too noisy to take a directional view.
Seven filings in eight weeks including a fresh board change suggest active corporate narrative, but filings look routine and sentiment impact is likely already absorbed.
Post-earnings -1.8% reaction on 2026-05-21 and no positive narrative catalyst since; sentiment drift remains negative.
Mild -1.0% earnings reaction in early May and quiet filing flow since suggest fading negative tone, but no clear positive inflection yet.
New material definitive agreement and direct financial obligation on 2026-06-10 could signal strategic expansion; filing tone is constructive and coverage volume is moderate.
Only two board-related filings in the period with no earnings or material agreements—sentiment signal is too thin to act on.

memos.headline: Collapsing Oil Prices and Flattening Curve Signal Shifting Geopolitical Risk Mix; NVDA and CAT Most Exposed
memos.body: I see a mixed but evolving geopolitical backdrop as of today. WTI crude has plunged 27.6% in one month to $72.67/bbl, suggesting either a demand shock or a significant easing of supply constraints—either way this reprices energy security risk and pressures petro-state leverage. The economic policy uncertainty index remains elevated at 273.74 but has fallen 13.9% over the past month, indicating that the acute phase of whatever policy shock drove it higher may be fading, though the 3-month change is flat, meaning the structural level of uncertainty is still well above historical norms. The VIX at 18.89 is up 13.9% over one month even as HY spreads are only marginally wider (+4bp), which tells me equity markets are pricing near-term event risk (possibly trade/sanctions-related) that credit markets have not yet validated. I have highest conviction on NVDA exposure to export-control risk given its recent 8-K filing and the persistent China-chip policy overhang, and on XOM where the oil collapse materially changes the energy-security calculus. A reversal of the oil decline or new export-control escalation would change my views.

views.note: Persistent US-China chip export-control risk remains the dominant structural geopolitical headwind; the June 18 8-K may relate to compliance or licensing developments, and elevated VIX suggests the market is pricing near-term event risk.

WTI's 27.6% one-month collapse to $72.67 reduces energy-security premium and compresses margins; I stay neutral rather than avoid because geopolitical supply disruptions could reverse the move quickly.
CAT's Reg FD disclosure on June 11 and its exposure to tariff/trade-policy risk keep me cautious, but the declining policy uncertainty index over one month tempers the downside call.

No new 8-K filings in the evidence window, but Apple's deep China manufacturing concentration remains a structural geopolitical vulnerability; the still-elevated policy uncertainty index keeps me from going long.

Multiple routine 8-K filings and a flattening but still positive yield curve (10y-2y at +31bp) suggest JPM is relatively insulated from geopolitical shocks; sanctions-enforcement activity could even be a revenue tailwind.
Three 8-K filings in six weeks suggest active corporate developments; regulatory/antitrust risk is structural but not acutely geopolitical, so I hold neutral pending clarity.

Roughly 35% cash reflects elevated VIX, sticky inflation, and broad tech weakness.
